behavioral_effects: An operator reading backend/.env.example or MANUAL_STEPS.md learns that the value must be set before a repository is activated, that empty is not a way to disable verification, and how to change it afterwards through the repository's GitHub webhook settings
compatibility_impact: None. No contract, interface, schema, or default changed. ENV_VARS.md and configuration.json move only because the .env.example comment is their source; the variable itself is unchanged.
follow_up: When the instance becomes publicly reachable, confirm a real delivery returns 200 under the repository's webhook Recent Deliveries and record the result
limitations: Documentation only; no mechanical guard was added. preflight-codecov still does not check this variable, deliberately — empty is a legitimate setting for a localhost-only instance, so a guard would block the common case
The described behaviour was verified by reading upstream source, not by observing a real GitHub delivery, which needs a publicly reachable instance
reason: backend/.env.example and MANUAL_STEPS.md describe CODECOV_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET as merely optional, which reads as safe to leave empty and safe to set at any time; both are wrong — Codecov bakes the value into the GitHub hook when the repository is activated, and an empty value produces a hook whose deliveries are rejected rather than a hook without verification, so an operator following the current wording gets silently non-functional webhooks
rollback: git revert, then make governance-sync to regenerate ENV_VARS.md and configuration.json. Nothing outside the repository is affected.
security_impact: None — documentation only, no code, compose, or configuration behaviour changed. It makes an existing security control legible: the wording previously implied an empty webhook secret meant unverified-but-working deliveries, when it actually yields a hook whose every delivery is rejected. No secret values are recorded; the variable stays placeholder-empty in the committed template.
summary: Document the webhook-secret ordering constraint and empty-value trap

read the upstream handler and worker code rather than the docs — apps/codecov-api/webhook_handlers/views/github.py validate_signature HMACs the raw body against github.webhook_secret and raises PermissionDenied when the signature is absent or mismatched, and apps/worker/services/repository.py create_webhook_on_provider posts the hook with that same secret in config.secret at activation time; the two call sites also carry different hardcoded fallbacks, so an absent key cannot work
